patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Medusa and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than OpenCart's shape. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than Medusa's shape. Workflow advantage differs because Medusa is shaped for Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 hig whereas OpenCart is shaped for GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud . Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Medusa and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax.; OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee.
- Company-size focus: Medusa (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs OpenCart (small-business, mid-market).
- Researched limits: Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0.

Limitations — Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce); OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting.

Poor-fit cases: Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · Avoid Medusa if you actually need OpenCart's motion (GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
